what_for.text: Synjardy is taken by mouth to treat type 2 diabetes in adults.
what_for.evidence: Synjardy contains two active substances empagliflozin and metformin. Each belongs to a group of medicines called “oral anti-diabetics”. These are medicines taken by mouth to treat type 2 diabetes.

what_for.text: It lowers the amount of sugar in your blood.
what_for.evidence: Thereby Synjardy lowers the amount of sugar in your blood.

what_for.text: This medicine can also help prevent heart disease.
what_for.evidence: This medicine can also help prevent heart disease.

how_to_use.text: The recommended dose is one tablet twice a day.
how_to_use.evidence: The recommended dose is one tablet twice a day.

how_to_use.text: Swallow the tablet whole with water.
how_to_use.evidence: Swallow the tablet whole with water.

how_to_use.text: Take the tablets with meals to lower your chance of an upset stomach.
how_to_use.evidence: Take the tablets with meals to lower your chance of an upset stomach.

how_to_use.text: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember.
how_to_use.evidence: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember.

how_to_use.text: If it is time for your next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not double.
how_to_use.evidence: If you do not remember until it is time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose of this medicine.

see_doctor_now.text: If you get symptoms of lactic acidosis, stop taking Synjardy and see a doctor immediately.
see_doctor_now.evidence: Stop taking Synjardy and contact a doctor or the nearest hospital immediately if you experience some of the symptoms of lactic acidosis

see_doctor_now.text: If face, lips, tongue or throat swell, contact a doctor or hospital straight away.
see_doctor_now.evidence: Contact a doctor or the nearest hospital straight away if you have any of the following side effects: ... Severe allergic reaction ... Possible signs of severe allergic reaction may include: ... swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat

see_doctor_now.text: If you get signs of diabetic ketoacidosis, stop taking Synjardy and see a doctor straight away.
see_doctor_now.evidence: contact a doctor or the nearest hospital straight away and stop taking this medicine until further advice from your doctor. These symptoms could be a sign of “diabetic ketoacidosis”

see_doctor_now.text: If you have pain, swelling or fever around your genitals, contact your doctor immediately.
see_doctor_now.evidence: Talk to your doctor immediately if you develop a combination of symptoms of pain, tenderness, redness, or swelling of the genitals or the area between the genitals and the anus with fever or feeling generally unwell.

side_effects.text: Low blood sugar is very common if taken with insulin or a sulphonylurea.
side_effects.evidence: Low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia), seen very commonly (may affect more than 1 in 10 people) ... If you take Synjardy with another medicine that can cause low blood sugar, such as a sulfonylurea or insulin, your risk of getting low blood sugar is increased.

side_effects.text: Urinary tract infections are common and can cause a burning feeling when passing urine.
side_effects.evidence: Urinary tract infection, seen commonly (may affect up to 1 in 10 people) ... The signs of urinary tract infection are: ... burning sensation when passing urine

side_effects.text: Feeling sick, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach ache and loss of appetite are very common.
side_effects.evidence: Very common ... feeling sick (nausea), vomiting ... diarrhoea or stomach ache ... loss of appetite

side_effects.text: Dehydration is uncommon and can cause thirst, lightheadedness or dizziness on standing.
side_effects.evidence: Dehydration, seen uncommonly (may affect up to 1 in 100 people) ... The signs of dehydration are not specific, but may include: ... unusual thirst ... lightheadedness or dizziness upon standing

storage.text: Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.
storage.evidence: Keep this medicine out of the sight and reach of children.

storage.text: Do not use after the expiry date on the packaging.
storage.evidence: Do not use this medicine after the expiry date which is stated on the blister and the carton after ‘EXP’.

storage.text: This medicine does not require any special storage conditions.
storage.evidence: This medicine does not require any special storage conditions.

storage.text: Do not use if packaging is damaged or shows signs of tampering.
storage.evidence: Do not use this medicine if you notice that the packaging is damaged or shows signs of tampering.
